newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court defers decision on Rao plea.
newsitem.headline: Indian court defers decision on Rao plea.

text.p: An Indian court said on Monday that it would rule later this week on a request by former Prime Minister P.V.Narasimha Rao for legal protection against arrest in a forgery case.
Delhi high court judge S.K. Mahajan said until he rules on Tuesday or Wednesday, a warrant for Rao's arrest issued last Friday will continue to be temporarily suspended.

A Delhi court issued a warrant to arrest Rao in the case last Friday, but he immediately won temporary reprieve by requesting anticipatory, or pre-emptive, bail which amounts to legal protection against arrest.

In the case, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) claims Rao was part of a conspiracy in 1989 to use forged documents to defame former Prime Minister V.P. Singh, who was then an opposition leader campaiging against Rao's party.
The case was one of three involving the former Congress party chief at the start of a week that analysts said could decide his political future.
If Rao is detained, he would be put in either judicial or police custody pending a hearing on the forgery case scheduled for October 14, court officials said.
